All projects →

Robot manipulation · Execution monitoring

CoMET

Did the robot actually grasp the ball? CoMET checks what should be true at each stage of a manipulation task. I use AHA’s FailGen to test how the monitor responds when an action goes wrong.

    Gaze & behavioural sensing · HRI 2025

    Gaze-Based Robot Failure Detection

    Investigating how gaze changes when a robot makes a mistake, and whether those changes can support early failure detection during collaborative tasks.

    • ROS
    • Random forest
    • 27 participants

    Trust & failure awareness · CHI 2026

    Trust Dynamics Across Multiple Robot Failures

    Examining how repeated robot failures affect trust, and when a robot's awareness of its mistakes helps people continue working with it.

    • Mixed-design study
    • Failure awareness
    • 54 participants

    Research focus

    Publications →

    I combine real-robot experiments, eye tracking, and controlled user studies to understand how people notice, interpret, and respond to robot mistakes. I also develop machine learning methods that combine vision–language models with robot-state monitoring to detect failures and guide recovery. My work connects human behaviour with robot intelligence to make human–robot collaboration more reliable.

    I am supervised by Wafa Johal and Vassilis Kostakos. My work is part of the Human-Computer Interaction Group and the Human-Robot Interaction Lab.

    Behavioural signals
    Using gaze and interaction patterns to detect when something goes wrong.
    Trust & recovery
    Understanding how repeated failures and robot awareness shape collaboration.
    Robotic systems
    Building and evaluating detection and recovery methods on real robots and in simulation.

    Teaching & supervision

    Teaching history →

    In Semester 2, 2026, I am a lab tutor for Intelligent Robotics (ECE4078) at Monash University and a marker for Usability Evaluation Methods (INFO20004) at the University of Melbourne. Previously, I tutored Elements of Data Processing (Semester 2, 2025 and Semester 1, 2026) and Machine Learning (Semester 1, 2026) at Melbourne.

    I also supervised a master's project developing a web application for annotating ROSBag data from March to July 2024.
